findings.issue: No test runner, no test script, and zero test files; the entire app is guarded only by the harness-owned acceptance suite in tests/
findings.suggestion: Add vitest plus unit coverage for lib/format.ts, compareRows, and the load* functions against fixture JSON from the API shape

findings.issue: Sort comparator implements spec-subtle rules (missing values last in both directions, numeric vs. lexical keys, aria-sort state) with no coverage; the obvious 'fix' of making missing values follow the direction would break spec silently
findings.suggestion: Unit-test compareRows directly: mixed missing/present values per column, ascending and descending

findings.issue: loadHome concentrates filtering (type slot either, generation), humanized substring search, 48-per-page slicing and page clamping with no tests; totalPages is 0 when count is 0 and the clamp diverges from the URL page
findings.suggestion: Unit-test loadHome against mocked apiGet: combined filters, empty results, page boundaries and page > totalPages

findings.issue: URL-state contract (defaults omitted, page reset on filter change, page=1 stripping) is only covered by one acceptance test; a refactor of updateSearch could break deep links and the reset rule
findings.suggestion: Add tests for validateSearch and the updateSearch search-mapper over representative URL shapes

findings.issue: The alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000) and species-vs-Pokémon ID mapping are duplicated across three code paths with no tests; inconsistency would break 'cards link to species pages' for forms like deoxys-normal
findings.suggestion: Extract one canonicalizePokemonRef helper and unit-test it with real and alternate-form IDs

findings.issue: apiGet throws on any non-404 and no route defines an errorComponent, so an API 500 renders a raw framework error; the error path is untested and unhandled
findings.suggestion: Add route-level errorComponent and a test that a 500 from the API renders a friendly page

findings.issue: evolutionNode recursion plus the nested-list rendering in pokemon.$name.tsx:39-52 handle branching chains (Eevee) with no coverage; a reshape of the tree or label logic would only be caught by one acceptance test
findings.suggestion: Unit-test evolutionNode against a branching chain fixture and assert the resulting tree

findings.issue: Display-name rules (humanize, dexNumber padding, latest-English selection, whitespace collapse, em dash for missing) are pure and trivially testable but untested; they affect every page
findings.suggestion: Cover each helper with table-driven unit tests, including edge cases like empty tokens, numeric 0 and null power

findings.issue: The in-memory TTL cache with in-flight dedup is subtle (a refactor could cache rejected promises or drop dedup, causing request storms); no tests pin its behaviour
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for memo: cache hit, TTL expiry, concurrent calls sharing one promise, rejected promises not cached

findings.issue: Server functions use identity validators ((data) => data), so nothing verifies that search params arriving from the client match the expected shape (e.g. page as string vs number)
findings.suggestion: Validate and coerce input in the validators, or type the validators properly, and test the coercion

summary: The agent wrote no tests at all: no runner, no script, no files, despite owning a data layer full of spec-encoded rules. Every risky area — filtering, pagination, sorting, URL state, alternate-form mapping, error handling — is guarded only by the acceptance suite it doesn't own. A small vitest suite over lib/format.ts, compareRows and the load* functions would have been cheap insurance for a codebase the team will maintain for years.
